howToUse: 1. Copy one entry's `prompt` field verbatim into fal.ai (nano banana / Gemini 2.5 Flash Image).
2. Save the returned image, then tell Claude which `id` it corresponds to and where the file was saved.

3. Claude will inspect the image with vision to confirm every letter actually printed on the image matches an item in that entry's `expectedLabels`, note (and skip, not guess) any duplicated/ambiguous printed letters, run `npm run images:webp` (from web/) to convert the source PNG to WebP in place, add/reuse an entry in the shared cross-skill registry `web/src/lib/photoImages.ts` (never inline the image/part data directly in a skill file), wire a multi-Bloom's-tier set of question branches into the skill file(s) named in `targetSkillFile` per RIGOR-STANDARDS.md, and verify (tsc + lint + a real request against the running dev server) before calling it done.

4. If any part is missing an arrow/letter, or a letter's arrow lands on the wrong structure, regenerate with a corrected prompt (add an explicit correction line naming the missing/misplaced part) rather than accepting a partial image — every part in `expectedLabels` must be identifiable.

5. An image is not tied to the one skill in `targetSkillFile` — once registered in photoImages.ts, reuse it from any other skill (same or different subject, same grade) that has a genuine curriculum reason to reference it, per curriculum-reference/CURRICULUM-MINING-GUIDE.md's photo-diagram section.
_meta.styleGuideSummary: All prompts embed the same style block so every generated image reads as one consistent visual system across the whole app — do not vary the style between images.
_meta.criticalRule: Every prompt instructs nano banana NOT to print any part's name as text anywhere on the image — only a circled capital letter + thin leader line per part. This is deliberate and different from typical stock 'labeled diagram' images (which usually print full text labels): text labels would give the answer away before the question is even asked. If a returned image has any part's name printed as text, it must be regenerated.
_meta.displayConstraint: Confirmed in web/src/components/visuals/Visual.tsx's PhotoDiagram renderer: images display at max-height 420px, max-width 672px (Tailwind max-w-2xl), object-contain, width 100% of container. Source images at roughly 1024-1200px on the long edge are plenty — this is never a print asset. The `dimensions` field on each entry below states the generation aspect ratio/size that best fits that constraint.

images.prompt: Create a clean, flat product-style illustration of a printed timetable board titled 'BUS TRAVEL TIMETABLE' in bold sans-serif capitals at the top. Do NOT print any extra labels beyond the table's own column headers and data — the column headers 'Destination'/'Departure'/'Arrival' are expected and required since a real timetable has them, but do not add any other explanatory text. images.prompt: Create a clean, flat-lay product-style illustration titled 'SHOPPING BUDGET AND RECEIPT' in bold sans-serif capitals at the top, showing TWO separate paper documents side by side on a fully solid plain light-grey background with a soft drop shadow under each. Style: soft studio lighting, realistic paper textures, no other clutter. LEFT document: a hand-ruled notebook-style budget list headed 'MY SHOPPING BUDGET' with 4 rows each listing a fictional planned item and a planned cost in KES (e.g. 'Sugar 1kg — KES 150', 'Rice 2kg — KES 300', 'Cooking oil 1L — KES 280', 'Bread — KES 65'), with an underlined total row at the bottom reading 'Total — KES 795'. RIGHT document: a printed monospace-font shop receipt headed with a fictional shop name (e.g. 'FRESH MART SUPERMARKET') listing the SAME 4 items but with their actual purchased cost (make 2 items match the budget exactly and 2 items differ slightly, e.g. sugar actually KES 160, cooking oil actually KES 260), a subtotal line, then on its OWN clearly separate line 'VAT 16% — KES ...', and then a bold total line further below reading 'TOTAL PAID — KES ...'. Mark EXACTLY 5 points, each with its own letter used only once: (A) one budgeted-item row on the left document, (B) ONLY the budget total row at the bottom of the left document (do not reuse B anywhere else), (C) one receipt item row on the right document, (D) ONLY the VAT line on the right document — this line must visibly exist and must be pointed to, it is the most important point in the whole image, (E) ONLY the total paid line at the very bottom of the receipt. Do NOT print any labels beyond what a real hand-written budget and a real printed receipt would naturally contain. No watermarks, no extra text. CRITICAL COMPLIANCE — READ CAREFULLY: the ONLY text permitted anywhere in the image is the title at the top and a single bold capital letter inside each circle. Do not print ANY other word, caption, name, or label anywhere in the image, even small captions beneath or beside an object. Each letter (A, B, C, D, E) must be used EXACTLY ONCE, pointing to exactly ONE distinct location — never reuse the same letter for a second, different point. Before finishing, proofread the title text character-by-character for correct spelling.

images.prompt: Create a clean, textbook-style educational anatomical illustration titled 'VIUNGO VYA MWILI VYA NDANI' at the top in bold sans-serif capitals — proofread this exact Swahili title character-by-character before finishing, it must read precisely 'VIUNGO VYA MWILI VYA NDANI' with no typos. Style: flat educational-diagram rendering (not photorealistic), soft muted colours, on a fully solid plain light-grey background. Draw a clean 3-row-by-3-column grid of 9 separate individually-outlined rounded-rectangle panels, evenly sized and evenly spaced with clear gaps between every panel so none touch. Each panel contains ONE simple, clearly recognisable organ icon, large and centred in its box, floating on a plain white panel background with no body outline or skeleton connecting the panels — each organ is fully independent of the others: PANEL 1 = a brain (grey-pink, folded texture). PANEL 2 = a heart (red, classic anatomical heart shape). PANEL 3 = a pair of lungs (pink, both lobes visible). PANEL 4 = a liver (deep red-brown, lobed shape). PANEL 5 = a spleen (purple, smaller bean-like shape, visually distinct from the liver and from the kidneys in panel 6 — the spleen and kidneys must look different from each other). PANEL 6 = a pair of kidneys (reddish-brown, bean-shaped). PANEL 7 = a bladder (pale pink/tan, small rounded sac). PANEL 8 = a single long bone (off-white, like a femur, with rounded knobby ends). PANEL 9 = a short segment of blood vessel (a red tube, possibly branching, NOT attached to any other organ, shown as its own standalone object like a piece of red tubing). For EACH of the 9 panels, draw a small solid black circle containing ONE bold white capital letter positioned in the corner of that panel — this is simply 9 independent labelled panels in a grid, not points on a shared figure, so there is no leader line needed, just the letter in the corner of each box. Use exactly these 9 letters, one per panel, reading left-to-right then top-to-bottom: PANEL 1 (brain) = A. PANEL 2 (heart) = B. PANEL 3 (lungs) = C. PANEL 4 (liver) = D. PANEL 5 (spleen) = E. PANEL 6 (kidneys) = F. PANEL 7 (bladder) = G. PANEL 8 (bone) = H. PANEL 9 (blood vessel) = I — this last panel MUST be labelled I, not H; a previous attempt incorrectly labelled BOTH panel 8 and panel 9 as 'H', which is wrong, panel 9 is a completely different letter, I. Do NOT print the name of any organ anywhere on the image — the only text allowed is the title and these 9 letters A through I, one per panel corner, each one of the 9 used exactly once with none repeated. No real photographic anatomy (this must read as a clean educational diagram, appropriate for a primary-school reading lesson), no people, no watermarks, no extra labels, no captions under any panel.

Wide landscape composition, 7 animals/birds arranged in a single row with even spacing, each shown as a clear side-profile or three-quarter-view full-body portrait large enough to see distinguishing features: (1) a brown-and-white COW standing calmly, (2) a PEACOCK with its colourful tail feathers fanned out, (3) a brown HORSE standing alert, (4) a grey ELEPHANT with large ears and tusks, (5) a HAWK with wings partly spread, perched, (6) a large stylised eagle-like mythical bird called GARUR with an impressive wingspan and regal posture (a majestic divine bird, not a real species — render it as a magnificent golden-brown eagle with unusually large wings), (7) a LION with a full mane, standing proudly. For EACH of the 7 animals, draw a thin dark-grey leader line from a small solid black circle positioned in the white space near that animal, containing a bold white capital letter (A through G, left to right), with the line's other end touching the animal it identifies. Do NOT print the name of any animal anywhere on the image — the only text allowed is the title and the 7 letters inside their circles. No watermarks, no extra labels, no human figures.
